Hi Olivia,

Thanks again for the quick sync this morning. Per our conversation, attached is a compact "zonal assertion" packet that summarizes how Redwood separates control/data planes and tenant workloads across Dedicated and Private deployments. The packet is intentionally short — one diagram and a mapping sheet that ties each diagram area to SIG/CQ control families.

Key points up front: 
- Control plane (management services, orchestration, model registry) runs in a separate VPC tied to the customer management account for Private; in Dedicated we host control plane services in a dedicated management tenancy with strict egress rules.
- Tenant inference workloads run in isolated enclaves (Dedicated: reserved GPU pools + ENI-per-tenant; Private: customer VPC with sidecar enforcement).
- Network demarcation is enforced with Transit Gateway routing rules, security group policies, and per-tenant KMS key scoping.
- Only TLS-terminated, authenticated API traffic is allowed across the demarcation; KV/cache replication uses mutually authenticated mTLS.

Attachments: zonal-assertion-diagram-v1.png, sig-mapping-sheet-v1.xlsx

Could you review the diagram and SIG mapping and let us know whether this level of detail is sufficient for Acme's SOC 2 / SIG intake? If helpful we can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough; I can make time next week (Mon/Tue preferred).

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu

Jasmine — looping in a few implementation specifics that address Olivia's ask (paste below for thread continuity). I'll also update the diagram and re-attach v2.

Control-plane custody and traffic: 
- Private deployments: control plane components (agent shims, management APIs) live in the customer's management VPC (customer account). Redwood provides a minimal control-plane package that the customer deploys; communication uses a mutually authenticated TLS channel to Redwood telemetry endpoints only for health/ops (no model data).
- Dedicated (Redwood-hosted) deployments: control plane services run in a dedicated management tenancy owned by Redwood; these services do not share host resources with tenant inference workloads. Egress from control plane is locked to management endpoints and our monitoring stack; all flows are logged to an immutable audit stream.

KMS/key custody: 
- Customer-managed keys: supported for data at rest and for model artifact encryption in Private deployments (customer KMS ARNs are referenced).
- Redwood-managed keys: used for platform operational artifacts in Hosted/Dedicated where customers opt-in. Key usage is scoped by IAM and by resource tags; we can provide a table mapping each storage surface to the KMS owner in the updated XLSX.

Network enforcement details to call out in the diagram: 
- Per-tenant ENIs (Dedicated) or VPC peering/Transit Gateway filters (Private)
- Security groups with least-privilege ingress (API ports only), egress denied by default
- Egress proxy for telemetry with allowlist destinations, TLS interception not performed

Action items from me: 1) update diagram to include control-plane inset + KMS legend; 2) produce sig-mapping-sheet-v2 with explicit KMS owner column; 3) ask Marcus Lin for final architecture sign-off (routing/ENI language).

I'll attach zonal-assertion-diagram-v2.png once updated.

Kimberly Park
